statement_record.book: A coproduct of A and B is an object A + B with injections ι_A : A → A + B, ι_B : B → A + B such that for every T and every pair f : A → T, g : B → T there is a unique [f, g] : A + B → T with ι_A ; [f, g] = f and ι_B ; [f, g] = g; [f, g] is the copairing.
statement_record.intree: `Notation "'Cocartesian' C" := (@Cartesian (C^op))` with `Coprod := @product_obj`, `merge f g := @fork _ O _ _ _ f g` (notation `f ▽ g`), `inl := @exl`, `inr := @exr`; the UMP is `ump_products ... : h ≈ fork f g ↔ (exl ∘ h ≈ f) * (exr ∘ h ≈ g)` read in C^op, with the two triangles surfacing as `f ▽ g ∘ inl ≈ f` and `f ▽ g ∘ inr ≈ g` and uniqueness as `merge_inv`.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — setoid rephrasing (≈ instead of =, and a biconditional UMP instead of an existence-plus-uniqueness statement) is faithful. The library obtains the coproduct by duality rather than as a primitive class, but the full API the book item needs (object, both injections, copairing, both triangles, uniqueness) is present.

evidence.intree_statement: Program Instance Sets_Cocartesian : @Cocartesian Sets := { product_obj := fun x y => {| carrier := (carrier x + carrier y)%type ; is_setoid := {| equiv := fun z w => match z with inl z => match w with inl w => z ≈ w | inr _ => False end | inr z => match w with inl _ => False | inr w => z ≈ w end end ... |} |} ; ... }.  The coproduct carrier is the sum type with cross-summand pairs identified with False, i.e. the disjoint union; the injections are Datatypes.inl / Datatypes.inr and the copairing is the case-split map.

Program Instance FinSet_Cocartesian : @Cocartesian FinSet := {| product_obj := fun m n => (m + n)%nat; fork := fun x y z (f : Fin.t y → Fin.t x) (g : Fin.t z → Fin.t x) p => match fin_split p with Datatypes.inl a => f a | Datatypes.inr b => g b end; exl := fun x y => Fin.L y; exr := fun x y => Fin.R x |}. statement_record.book: For f : A → X and g : A → Y with common domain, the pushout X +_A Y is the colimit of the span: an object with ι_X : X → X +_A Y, ι_Y : Y → X +_A Y such that (a) f ; ι_X = g ; ι_Y and (b) for every T with x : X → T, y : Y → T satisfying f ; x = g ; y there is a unique t with ι_X ; t = x and ι_Y ; t = y. Such a square is a pushout square; ι_X is the pushout of g along f.

Lemma iso_pullback_stable {C : Category} {x y z : C} (f : x ~> z) (m : y ~> z) (Hm : IsIsomorphism m) (P : Pullback f m) : IsIsomorphism (pullback_fst f m P).  Instantiated at C^op — where `IsPushout f g := @Pullback (C^op) ...` — this yields the invertibility half of Example 6.23: the pushout of an isomorphism along any morphism is again an isomorphism. It is only ever stated in the pullback direction; no pushout restatement exists.

statement_record.book: For f : A → X and isomorphisms i : A → A', j : X → X', put f' := i⁻¹ ; f ; j. Then the square with sides f, i, j, f' is a pushout square, so X' is a pushout X +_A A'; the mediator out of any competing cocone (x, a) with f ; x = i ; a is forced to be j⁻¹ ; x, which is checked to commute and be unique.
statement_record.intree: No general lemma. The nearest assertions are (i) the identity case inside the cospans double category: `luni_map_in1` + `Cospan_dunit_left_from_to` exhibit `pushout_apex PL ≅ cospan_apex h` for `PL` the CHOSEN pushout of `cospan_in2 h` along `id[b]`; and (ii) the dual invertibility statement `iso_pullback_stable`, which at C^op says a pushout of an isomorphism is an isomorphism.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker in three separate ways. (1) Direction of the claim: the book CONSTRUCTS a pushout square out of two isos with no ambient existence hypothesis; both in-tree results instead ASSUME a pushout exists (a `HasPushouts C` context, or a given `Pullback`) and then compare it to something. (2) Generality: the Cospan/Double witnesses cover only i = id, not an arbitrary isomorphism, and only for spans whose legs are cospan legs. (3) `iso_pullback_stable` is a strictly weaker consequence — it concludes that a morphism is invertible, not that a square is universal, and Example 6.23 implies it but not conversely.

evidence.intree_statement: Program Instance FinSet_HasPushouts : HasPushouts FinSet := { pushout := fun x y z f g => {| Pull := po_apex f g; pullback_fst := po_in1 f g; pullback_snd := po_in2 f g |} }.  Here `po_apex := fin_countP po_isrep` (line 406) is the NUMBER OF CONNECTED COMPONENTS of the graph on the coproduct `y + z` whose edges are `po_edges := map (fun i => (po_src i, po_dst i)) (all_fin x)` with `po_src i := fin_join (inl (f i))`, `po_dst i := fin_join (inr (g i))` (lines 390-395), and the injections `po_in1 i := po_cls (fin_join (inl i))`, `po_in2 j := po_cls (fin_join (inr j))` (425-427) are the class maps of the coproduct injections. That is exactly the book's "disjoint union modulo the equivalence generated by f(a) ~ g(a)" / "connected components of X ⊔ Y".

Program Instance Sets_HasPushouts : HasPushouts Sets := {| pushout := fun X Y Z f g => {| Pull := pushout_apex_setoid f g; pullback_fst := pushout_inl_mor f g; pullback_snd := pushout_inr_mor f g; ... |} |}.  The apex carrier is `Datatypes.sum (carrier B) (carrier C)` equipped with `pushout_eq` (line 51), the inductively GENERATED equivalence whose constructors are exactly `po_inl_cong`, `po_inr_cong`, `po_glue : pushout_eq (inl (f a)) (inr (g a))`, `po_sym`, `po_trans` — the literal "reflexive, symmetric, transitive closure of f(a) ~ g(a) on the disjoint union".
Lemma po_commutes (i : Fin.t x) : po_in1 (f i) = po_in2 (g i).  The glueing clause: each element i of A does identify f(i) in X with g(i) in Y inside the apex.

statement_record.book: FinSet has all pushouts: the pushout of f : A → X and g : A → Y is the set of equivalence classes of X ⊔ Y under the equivalence relation generated by f(a) ~ g(a) for a ∈ A; equivalently the set of connected components of X ⊔ Y with a connection for each a ∈ A.
statement_record.intree: `FinSet_HasPushouts : HasPushouts FinSet` with apex `po_apex = fin_countP po_isrep`, the count of connected components of the graph on `y + z` with one edge `(inl (f i), inr (g i))` per i, computed by a union-find labelling (`components`/`po_lab`), the injections being the class maps of the coproduct injections. Companion: `Sets_HasPushouts : HasPushouts Sets` with the apex the sum-type carrier under the inductively generated equivalence `pushout_eq` (glue constructor `po_glue`, plus symmetry/transitivity/congruences).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, and on the FinSet side intree-stronger in one respect: the skeletal presentation forces the apex to be a natural number, so the construction actually COMPUTES the number of equivalence classes (the file header, line 26-34, states precisely this: "What is required here is the connected-components computation ... which this file performs by a union-find labeling"). The Sets version realizes the book's "equivalence relation generated by" clause literally, and is funext-free because the equivalence is carried by the setoid rather than by a quotient type.
